project: Daly et al. (2025) named major-structure reconstruction, version 2

policy.naming_rule: A published abbreviation is linked to geometry only where label placement, the heavy printed trace, and local trace topology support a unique association. Proximity alone is insufficient.
policy.connectivity_rule: Segments are ordered by cartographic continuity. Straight gap bridges are stored separately and never presented as observed fault geometry.
policy.prohibited_evidence: Mineral occurrences, deposit density, exploration history and deposit-proximity scores were not used to name, connect, rank or classify structures.

confidence_definitions.high: Label and unique heavy trace are directly associated and local topology supports the link.
confidence_definitions.medium: Association is supported but requires an interpreted offset or continuation across closely spaced linework.
confidence_definitions.medium_low: Plausible association exists, but continuity or uniqueness is not fully demonstrated.
confidence_definitions.unresolved: The label cannot be uniquely associated with a continuous printed trace.

policy.stroke_width_note: Printed stroke width is a cartographic fault-zone symbol, not physical fault-zone width.

Northward branch of the same mapped network.

structures.name: Lwawa

centerline_parts.reason: Long trace adjacent to the western Mwashia belt and the LB label.
Parallel strand converges with the main trace at a mapped endpoint and is retained as part of the labelled fault zone.

notes: Caption spelling Lwawa is canonical; Lwawu is an alias.
The name is not applied to adjacent Mwinilunga 0011.
